sentences.text:
on 13 April,
2022
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Tarlada Rajasekhar Rao
 Crl.R.C.No.295 of 2013
Order:

-
The Food Inspector, Division-I, Kadapa District filed the complaint against the accused under Section.7(V) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, "the Act") r/w Rules.49(28)
and 50(1) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short, "the Rules") punishable under Section.16(1)(a)(ii) of the Act.

2. On 09.01.2010 at about 12:30 P.M. LW.1, G.Sreesailam, Food Inspector along with his office subordinate Sri Seetharamaiah and Tahsildar of Chennur by name Smt B. Santhamma visited M/s.
Thulasi Packaged Drinking water i.e., the premises of the petitioner/accused herein and found that the accused was present and he was transacting business and manufacturing Thulasi Packaged Drinking Water for sale for human consumption.
LW1 Food Inspector disclosed his identity and the purpose of inspection and called one mediator namely S. Md.Waris.

In the presence of the mediator,
the Food Inspector inspected the said water unit and found that they were manufacturing 200 ml sealed water packets and filling 20 litres cans of Thulasi Packaged Drinking Water.

On enquiry,
about the purpose for which they were manufacturing the water packets and filling the cans, it is stated that it is for the sale to the public for human consumption.
3. Then the Food Inspector also enquired the accused with regard to obtaining the B.I.S. certificate and P.F.A. License.
The accused stated that he is having no objection certificate from the Gram Panchayat, Chennur Village and they are not having any B.I.S. certificate and P.F.A. license.
Then the Food Inspector drafted panchanama as per procedure and filed the charge sheet.

4. Basing on the charge sheet, the Court of learned I Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate,
Kadapa conducted the trial and convicted the accused vide judgment dated 14.06.2011.

entities.text:
I Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate,
Kadapa
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 5. The contention of the petitioner is that he has not obtained B.I.S. certificate and P.F.A. license.

The evidence of PW1 coupled with Ex P5 shows that, when PW1 went along with Tahsildar,
Chennur, he observed the accused manufacturing packaged drinking water in sealed packets and 20 litres cans.
6.
Heard both sides.

7. The learned trial Court, relying on the judgment in "Krishna Foods & Acqua Minerals, Nallajerla and others Vs. Government of India, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Department of Health)
T. Shafiulla, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., on 13 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10218592/
1 and another," reported in 2004 (6) ALT 4 (D.B.), which stated that, for the manufacture, sale or exhibition for sale of packaged drinking water, a certification mark from the Bureau of Indian Standards is mandatory.
8.

entities.text:
Krishna Foods & Acqua Minerals, Nallajerla and others Vs. Government of India, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Department of Health)
T. Shafiulla, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., on 13 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned Judge, after considering the material on record and the relying on the documentary evidence i.e., Ex P3 to Ex P5 found that the accused, being the Proprietor of M/s. Thulasi Packaged Drinking Water is manufacturing the water packets and filling the cans without obtaining B.I.S.
Certificate and P.F.A. license, which is mandatory as per the Act.

9. Hence, the trial Court vide judgment dated 14.06.2011, found the accused guilty for the offences under Section.7(V) of the Act r/w Rules.49(28) and 50(1) of the Rules and found him punishable under Section.16(1)(a)(ii) of the Act and sentenced him to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of six (6) months and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- (Rupees one thousand only).
In default of payment of fine, he was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one month.
10. Aggrieved by the said judgment, the petitioner filed Criminal Appeal No.91 of 2011 on the file of the Court of the learned VI Additional Sessions Judge, Kadapa.
The appeal was dismissed confirming the judgment and conviction of sentence imposed by the trial Court in C.C.No.250 of 2010 dated 14.06.2011.

11. Aggrieved by the same, the present Criminal Revision Case is filed before this Court stating that there is no evidence of proof that the packed water was sold in the market and that any complaint by consumer against the manufacturer is given.
He contended that without there being any complaint given by the consumer, the said complaint is not maintainable against the manufacturing unit.
12. Learned counsel for the petitioner has not raised any valid grounds muchless the question of law was not involved in the afore mentioned grounds.
The trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court, after considering the evidence and relying on the judgment stated supra convicted the accused for the said offences.

Admittedly, the petitioner has been manufacturing and selling the water packets and filling the cans without obtaining B.I.S. Certificate and P.F.A. license, which are stated to be mandatory as per the provisions of the Act.
It is trite law that this Court while exercising jurisdiction under sections 397 and 401 Cr.P.C. cannot re-appreciate the evidence.
13. Hence, I found no reasons to interfere with the judgment passed by the trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court.
14. Accordingly, the Criminal Revision Case is dismissed.
Bail stands cancelled and the Registry is directed to send the record to the trial Court.

Pending Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
